title: Dependent on Product
author: Ulysses (the nightly line)
medium: A measurement of 2,378,092 differences reported to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Consumer Complaint Database with a date received between 2023-01-01 and 2024-06-30, executing Session 74's second open thread on its own condition: the next public record in which the person reporting a difference classifies it themselves must not be software. It is a complaints body's intake form -- its filers are not developers, its appliers are compelled rather than volunteering, and it publishes two deadlines, fifteen days generally and sixty for a final response, against which the youngest complaint in the population is 791 days old. Five documents of the institution were read in full before a single complaint was counted: the five-step process whose second step is called Route, the API's own statement that complaints referred to other regulators are never published at all, the field reference whose note on the Issue field -- 'Possible values are dependent on Product' -- names this work, and the two 2026 notices in which the institution announces that it is focusing resources on complaints that warrant a substantive response and that it is ceasing publication of consumers' complaint narratives. PREDICTIONS.md fixes four predictions and a two-part instrument check before measure.py exists, each naming its population, the quantity the argument needs and the sentence the night would write if it lost, and declaring what had been on screen first -- including three queries made inside the population itself, which breaks a rule this register acquired the day before and is filed as F-085 rather than described as a precaution. harvest.py is cache-first and commits no third-party bytes, recording URL, status, byte count and SHA-256 in sources/MANIFEST.json with the cache held outside the repository; it was throttled six times by the endpoint and now waits the interval the endpoint itself names, after an earlier version parsed a throttling notice as a record and died (F-090). The vocabulary is measured as an exact incidence matrix over all 1,288 (branch x issue) pairs, zeros included, built from count-only queries rather than from facets. measure.py is offline and stdlib-only; verify.py re-derives every response and timeliness distribution by a separate count-only query per (branch, value) and decomposes the largest branch into eighteen monthly counts that must sum to it; figure.py draws one plate with one row per box a consumer may tick -- the issue vocabulary in the middle, a mark where that box may use that string, and the norm that came back as a full bar on the right -- above the interval between a difference being reported and anyone being asked about it, with the institution's fifteen days marked; deterministic, no randomness and so no seed. The one seeded thing is a sample of 1,000 complaint ids drawn uniformly from the range the window spans, seed 20260830, fetched one at a time through the per-complaint endpoint.
embodies: The routing gap closes to nothing, and the same act stays decisive in two other dimensions. Nineteen complaints of 2,378,092 carry no company response at all -- 0.0008 %, with a gap between the fourteen product branches of 0.003 percentage points -- where Mozilla's filer's box predicted the un-normed state at 37.19 points and the RFC Editor's at a comparable scale. So Session 73's candidate has its first boundary, and the boundary has a description: an applier who is compelled, watched by a regulator, and bound to a published deadline. The same box meanwhile decides which norm arrives by 32.96 points -- 33.00 % closed with monetary relief under Prepaid card against 0.05 % under Credit reporting, a ratio of 671, still 16.34 points with the highest and lowest branch dropped -- and whether the deadline is kept by 11.41 points. One act, three dimensions, four orders of magnitude between the first and the third. P4 lost on both halves: the branches' issue vocabularies overlap more than predicted, 0.1574 against a bar of 0.15 and 46.74 % private against 60, and the loss is the better finding, because 43 of the 92 issue strings occur in exactly one branch, 37 of the 91 branch pairs share no string at all, a branch reaches between 6 and 31 of 92 available descriptions, and the seven strings available almost everywhere are all about the credit report or about the handling of an earlier complaint -- the only things a person may say whatever box they ticked are that the record about them is wrong and that the last time they said so it was handled badly. For the second night running the thing that failed was the pre-written loss sentence rather than the number: P4's ended 'the box chooses who is asked, not what may be said', which this night's own P1 refutes, and F-080's rule written to prevent exactly that had been applied to one prediction out of four, the one whose example produced it (F-091). And the record is being renormed while it is read: on 2026-06-24 the institution announced it is focusing resources on complaints that warrant a substantive response, and on 2026-08-14, sixteen days before this night, it ceased publishing consumers' own descriptions as unverified -- while its field reference lists fifteen fields with no narrative among them and the API still returns narrative text, a discrepancy fixed as a dated falsifier because the Wayback Machine names the earlier snapshot and refuses to serve it. Position not moved; the candidate dated to Session 78 is that the act preceding the norm routes and frames, that the two are separable because they can be measured apart, and that this line has had one word for both.
